question: The four IMNCI clinical signs used to classify dehydration severity are: general condition (restless/lethargic), eyes (sunken or not), skin pinch return (normal/slow/very slow), and ability to drink (able/drinking poorly/unable to drink).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. IMNCI uses exactly four clinical signs: general condition, eyes, skin pinch return, and drinking ability. Two or more signs from the 'some dehydration' cluster → Plan B; two or more from the 'severe' cluster → Plan C. Accurate knowledge of which signs constitute each cluster prevents dangerous under- or over-treatment.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. These are the four IMNCI dehydration assessment signs. Classification: No signs = No dehydration (Plan A); ≥2 of [restless/irritable, sunken eyes, slow skin pinch, drinks eagerly/thirsty] = Some Dehydration (Plan B: 75 mL/kg ORS over 4 h); ≥2 of [lethargic/unconscious, very sunken eyes, very slow skin pinch, unable to drink] = Severe Dehydration (Plan C: 100 mL/kg IV Ringer's lactate).
